title: Onimusha: Way of the Sword Demo
provenance: Reported by flacknabe-cpu (highball-db#450, 2026-10-11), Apple M1 Pro, macOS 26.7, Highball 0.10.14, engine x64-sikarugir10.0_6-r24, the game on D3DMetal in a DXMT environment, 60 fps cap, rated 3 of 5 after 19 minutes, the game's benchmark at 11341 points and 32 fps on average with a modified D3DMetal. flacknabe-cpu again (highball-db#450, 2026-10-16): Highball 0.10.16, engine x64-crossover26.3-r25, the original D3DMetal 3, HB_TSSHIM_ATOMIC64=1, the demo launches and reaches gameplay on the M1 Pro. Not verified by the maintainer.
notes: Capcom's RE Engine, DirectX 12. On an M1 Pro it stops with an unsupported graphics card error, because D3DMetal answers no to the game's check for 64-bit atomics on descriptor heap resources (D3D12 OPTIONS11), the same check that blocks Kunitsu-Gami. A player got it running, through its benchmark at 32 fps, by patching D3DMetal itself so the check says yes. Highball cannot ship a modified D3DMetal, so out of the box it does not start on an M1. On an M4 D3DMetal 3 already answers yes (measured here 2026-10-14 with a probe). On Highball's Wine 11 engine r25 (0.10.16) the variable HB_TSSHIM_ATOMIC64=1 makes Highball's DirectX 12 layer answer yes, and the demo reaches gameplay on the M1 Pro with the original D3DMetal (confirmed by the reporter, highball-db#450). The recipe sets both; the game's benchmark has its own page. PRAGMATA SKETCHBOOK's demo stops at the same check and ran with the same D3DMetal patch (highball-db#485).

knownIssues.symptom: Unsupported graphics card error at start, then the game quits (M1 Pro)
knownIssues.cause: D3DMetal reports AtomicInt64OnDescriptorHeapResourceSupported as false, and the game requires it
knownIssues.fix: the recipe: Wine 11 engine r25 or later with HB_TSSHIM_ATOMIC64=1, which has Highball's layer in front of D3DMetal answer yes (confirmed on an M1 Pro, highball-db#450)
